name: ChatGPT
description: OpenAI's assistant app: chat, voice, image generation, deep research, study mode and custom GPTs.
why: The most widely used AI assistant, with the broadest feature set and a strong free tier.

name: Claude
description: Anthropic's assistant on web, desktop and mobile: writing, analysis, artifacts, projects, connectors and skills.
why: Excellent at careful writing, long documents and analysis, and it can use skills and connectors to your tools.
bestFor: build small interactive tools in chat

name: Gemini
description: Google's assistant, built into Search, Gmail, Docs and Android, with Guided Learning and Deep Research.
why: Best if you live in Google's apps, and it has a generous free tier.
bestFor: ai inside google docs and gmail

name: NotebookLM
description: Google's research notebook that answers only from sources you upload, with citations, audio overviews and study aids.
why: Grounded in your own material with citations, which makes it the safest AI tool for studying and research.

name: Perplexity
description: Answer engine that searches the web and cites its sources.
why: The quickest way to get a researched answer with links you can check.

name: LangGraph
description: Build stateful, multi-step agents as graphs with persistence, human-in-the-loop and streaming.
why: The most battle-tested choice for production agents that need explicit control flow, retries and durable state.

learn.title: LangChain Academy: Intro to LangGraph (free course)

name: Claude Agent SDK
description: The harness behind Claude Code as a library: tools, subagents, MCP, hooks and context management.
why: Gives you a proven general-purpose agent loop with file, shell and web tools built in, so you skip writing the loop yourself.
bestFor: agent that edits files and runs commands

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: Lightweight SDK for agents with handoffs, guardrails, sessions and built-in tracing.
why: Very few concepts to learn. Handoffs between specialist agents and tracing work out of the box.

name: Pydantic AI
description: Type-safe agent framework from the Pydantic team, with structured outputs and dependency injection.
why: Feels like FastAPI for agents: typed, testable and model-agnostic. Ideal if you live in typed Python.

name: Google ADK
description: Agent Development Kit for building, evaluating and deploying agents, optimized for Gemini and Vertex AI.
why: Best path if you deploy on Google Cloud. Evaluation and deployment tooling are first-class.

name: Mastra
description: TypeScript framework for agents, workflows, RAG, memory and evals, with a local dev playground.
why: The most complete batteries-included agent framework for TypeScript teams.

name: Vercel AI SDK
description: TypeScript toolkit for streaming chat UIs, tool calling and agents across every major provider.
why: The standard for putting a streaming AI chat into a React or Next.js app. One API, any provider.

name: DSPy
description: Program LLMs instead of prompting them: declarative modules plus automatic prompt optimization.
why: Unique: it optimizes prompts against your metric automatically instead of you hand-tuning them.

name: Model Context Protocol
description: The open standard for connecting AI apps to tools, data and prompts.
why: Start here. Every major AI client supports it, so a tool you build once works in all of them.

learn.title: Official guide: build your first MCP server

name: FastMCP
description: The Pythonic way to build MCP servers and clients with decorators, auth and deployment helpers.
why: The fastest route from a Python function to a production MCP server. A few lines per tool.

name: MCP TypeScript SDK
description: Official TypeScript SDK for MCP servers and clients.
why: The reference implementation. New spec features land here first.

name: MCP Inspector
description: Visual tool for testing and debugging MCP servers.
why: The one debugging tool every MCP author needs: call tools by hand and inspect the raw messages.

name: MCP Registry
description: The official registry for discovering and publishing MCP servers.
why: The canonical index the clients themselves read. Publish here to be discoverable.

name: GitHub MCP Server
description: GitHub's official server: issues, PRs, code search and Actions for agents.
why: Official, well-maintained and covers almost all of the GitHub API that agents need.

name: Playwright MCP
description: Let agents drive a real browser through accessibility snapshots, with no vision model needed.
why: Reliable browser control for any MCP client, built by the Playwright team.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
description: Gives coding agents Chrome DevTools: inspect DOM and CSS, read console and network, record performance traces.
why: Lets your agent actually see and debug the page it just built instead of guessing.

name: Context7
description: Feeds up-to-date, version-specific library docs into your coding agent.
why: Fixes the biggest cause of bad AI code: outdated API knowledge.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal, IDEs, desktop and web.
why: Strong at multi-file changes across large codebases, and extensible with MCP, hooks, skills and subagents.
bestFor: agent that writes code across repo

name: Cursor
description: AI-first code editor (VS Code fork) with agent mode and best-in-class tab completion.
why: The most polished all-in-one AI editor. The easiest switch for VS Code users.

name: OpenAI Codex
description: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for the terminal, IDE and cloud.
why: Open-source CLI with sandboxed execution by default. Pairs with cloud tasks that run in parallel.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal agent powered by Gemini.
why: A generous free tier and a very long context window. The best zero-cost entry point.

name: GitHub Copilot
description: AI pair programmer in VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub, plus a cloud coding agent that opens PRs.
why: Works in the editor you already use and is approved at most companies.

name: Cline
description: Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code; bring your own model and key.
why: The best open-source agent inside VS Code. Transparent, with no markup on tokens.

name: Aider
description: AI pair programming in your terminal with tight git integration.
why: Every change is a clean git commit, and it works with almost any model.

name: Zed
description: High-performance editor in Rust with a built-in agent panel that can host external agents.
why: The fastest editor around, and it's open source. Can host Claude Code, Gemini CLI and others.

name: Figma MCP Server
description: Figma's official MCP server: gives coding agents your frames, components, variables and styles.
why: The highest-fidelity way to turn a real design into code, because the agent reads the design itself, not a screenshot.

name: shadcn/ui
description: Copy-in React components on Radix and Tailwind, with a registry and MCP server that agents can install from.
why: The component library AI tools generate best, because the code is yours and every model knows it.
bestFor: ui components for ai generated apps

name: v0
description: Vercel's prompt-to-app builder for React/Next.js UIs, with one-click deploy.
why: The best UI quality from a prompt, and it outputs real code you can take with you.

name: Lovable
description: Build full-stack web apps by chatting, with a database, auth and hosting included.
why: Gets non-developers from idea to a working full-stack app fastest.

name: Google Stitch
description: Google Labs tool that generates UI designs and front-end code from text or sketches, with Figma export.
why: Strong at exploring several visual directions fast before you commit to code.

name: Dembrandt
description: Extract any website's design system (colors, type, spacing, motion, components) as design tokens; CLI plus MCP server.
why: One command turns a live site into Tailwind, shadcn or W3C tokens, so your agent matches a real brand instead of guessing.
bestFor: copy a website's colors and fonts

name: OpenRouter
description: One API key and OpenAI-compatible endpoint for hundreds of models, with automatic fallbacks.
why: Try any model by changing one string. No new accounts, contracts or SDKs.
bestFor: try many llms with one key

name: Claude API
description: Anthropic's API for the Claude models: tool use, prompt caching, batch and agent tooling.
why: A frontier model family that is especially strong at coding, agents and long, careful work.

name: OpenAI API
description: GPT models, Responses API, realtime voice, images and embeddings.
why: The broadest single platform: text, realtime voice, images and embeddings in one place.

name: Gemini API
description: Google's multimodal models with very long context, via AI Studio or Vertex AI.
why: The best price for long context and video/audio understanding, with a real free tier.

name: LiteLLM
description: Call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format; self-hosted proxy with budgets, keys and fallbacks.
why: The self-hosted answer to 'one gateway for every team and provider', with cost controls.

name: Groq
description: Very low-latency inference for open models on custom LPU hardware.
why: When latency matters most, like voice or autocomplete, it's among the fastest options.

name: Hugging Face Hub
description: The home of open models and datasets, plus Inference Providers and Spaces.
why: Where every open model is published. Unavoidable and excellent.

name: Ollama
description: Run open models locally with one command and an OpenAI-compatible API.
why: The simplest way to run a model locally, and most tools integrate with it.

name: LM Studio
description: Desktop app to discover, download and chat with local models, with a local API server.
why: The best GUI for local models, with clear hints about which models fit your hardware.
bestFor: chatgpt offline on mac or windows

name: llama.cpp
description: The C/C++ engine behind most local inference; runs GGUF models on CPU and GPU.
why: Maximum control and portability. It runs anywhere, including phones and Raspberry Pi.

name: MLX
description: Apple's array framework for fast inference and fine-tuning on Apple silicon.
why: The fastest way to run and fine-tune models on a Mac.

name: vLLM
description: High-throughput, memory-efficient serving engine for LLMs in production.
why: The default open-source way to serve models to many users on GPUs.

name: SGLang
description: Fast serving framework for LLMs and vision models with structured generation.
why: Often the fastest engine for large models and structured-output-heavy workloads.

name: Open WebUI
description: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style UI for Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API.
why: The most feature-complete self-hosted chat UI, with RAG, users and tools included.

name: Docling
description: Convert PDFs, Office files and images into clean Markdown/JSON with layout and tables preserved.
why: Best open-source parsing quality for complex PDFs, and it runs fully locally.

name: MarkItDown
description: Microsoft utility that turns almost any file into LLM-ready Markdown.
why: Tiny and dependable. The quickest fix for 'get this file into a prompt'.
bestFor: convert word excel powerpoint to markdown

name: LlamaIndex
description: Framework for RAG and agents over your data: connectors, indexing, retrieval and workflows.
why: The deepest toolkit for retrieval specifically: loaders, chunking, rerankers and query engines.

name: Sentence Transformers
description: Compute embeddings and rerank with thousands of pretrained models.
why: The standard library for open embeddings and rerankers, locally and for free.

name: pgvector
description: Vector similarity search inside Postgres.
why: If you already run Postgres you probably don't need a separate vector database.

name: Qdrant
description: High-performance vector search engine in Rust with rich filtering.
why: The best dedicated open-source vector DB when you outgrow Postgres or need heavy filtering.

name: Chroma
description: Developer-friendly embedding database that runs in-process or in the cloud.
why: The lowest friction for prototypes: pip install and go.

name: LanceDB
description: Serverless, embedded multimodal vector database on the Lance columnar format.
why: Embedded like SQLite but handles images, video and huge datasets on cheap object storage.

name: Pinecone
description: Fully managed serverless vector database.
why: Zero ops. Pick it when you'd rather pay than run infrastructure.

name: Mem0
description: Memory layer that lets agents remember users and facts across sessions.
why: The simplest way to add personalization memory to any agent or chatbot.

name: Letta
description: Platform for stateful agents with self-editing memory (formerly MemGPT).
why: Agents that manage their own memory over months, a research idea that is now production-ready.

name: Graphiti
description: Real-time temporal knowledge graphs for agent memory, by Zep.
why: Tracks how facts change over time, which flat vector memory can't do.

name: Langfuse
description: Open-source LLM engineering platform: tracing, prompt management, datasets and evals.
why: The best open-source, self-hostable all-rounder that works with any framework.

learn.title: Hamel Husain: Your AI product needs evals

name: promptfoo
description: CLI for testing prompts, comparing models and red-teaming; config-driven and CI-friendly.
why: Unit tests for prompts that run in CI, plus serious red-teaming. Great for engineers.

name: Braintrust
description: Evals, prompt playground and production logging for AI products.
why: The most polished eval workflow for teams where product managers and engineers both iterate.

name: LangSmith
description: Tracing, evaluation and deployment from the LangChain team; works with any framework.
why: The deepest integration if you build on LangGraph or LangChain.

name: Arize Phoenix
description: Open-source observability and evals built on OpenTelemetry.
why: Vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry tracing that runs in a notebook or self-hosted.

name: Ragas
description: Metrics and test-set generation for evaluating RAG pipelines.
why: The standard metrics for answering 'is my RAG actually retrieving the right thing?'

name: Inspect
description: UK AI Security Institute framework for rigorous LLM and agent evaluations.
why: Research-grade evals with sandboxed agent tasks. Used by frontier safety teams.

name: Firecrawl
description: Turn any website into LLM-ready Markdown or structured data; crawl, map and extract.
why: Handles JavaScript, anti-bot measures and whole-site crawls, so it just works on real websites.

name: Crawl4AI
description: Open-source, LLM-friendly web crawler and scraper.
why: The best fully free, self-hosted option for scraping at scale.

name: Tavily
description: Search API built for agents and RAG, returning ready-to-use content.
why: Returns clean, relevant content rather than a list of links. The default search tool for agents.

name: Exa
description: Neural web search API for finding pages by meaning.
why: Finds pages by meaning ('companies like X'), which keyword search engines can't.

name: Browser Use
description: Open-source library that lets AI agents operate a browser to complete tasks.
why: The most popular open-source way to give an agent a browser.

name: Stagehand
description: Browser automation that mixes Playwright code with natural-language actions.
why: More reliable than fully autonomous agents: write code where you can, use AI where you must.

name: E2B
description: Secure cloud sandboxes (Firecracker microVMs) for running AI-generated code.
why: The standard for safely running code that an LLM wrote. Starts in milliseconds.

name: Daytona
description: Fast, elastic sandboxes for running AI-generated code; self-hostable.
why: A strong alternative to E2B when you need self-hosting or long-lived sandboxes.

name: Modal
description: Serverless GPUs, sandboxes and functions; deploy Python in seconds.
why: The nicest developer experience for running GPU workloads without managing servers.

name: Instructor
description: Structured outputs from LLMs using Pydantic models, with validation and retries.
why: The simplest dependable way to get validated JSON from any provider.

name: Outlines
description: Guaranteed structured generation by constraining tokens to a JSON schema, regex or grammar.
why: Makes invalid output impossible on open models, instead of retrying until it's valid.

name: BAML
description: A small language for typed LLM functions, with tests and a live playground.
why: Treats prompts as typed functions you can test, and generates clients for many languages.

name: Unsloth
description: Fine-tune and run RL on open models about 2x faster with much less VRAM; free Colab notebooks.
why: The fastest way to fine-tune on a single GPU, and the docs teach you how as you go.
bestFor: fine tune llm on one gpu
fine tune for free on colab

learn.title: Unsloth docs: fine-tuning guide for beginners

name: Axolotl
description: YAML-configured fine-tuning for many architectures, methods and multi-GPU setups.
why: Reproducible, config-driven training that scales to many GPUs.

name: TRL
description: Hugging Face library for SFT, DPO, GRPO and other post-training methods.
why: The reference implementations of post-training methods, which most other tools build on.

name: Weights & Biases
description: Experiment tracking for training runs, plus Weave for LLM app traces.
why: The default for tracking and comparing training runs.

name: LiveKit Agents
description: Framework for realtime voice and video AI agents over WebRTC, including telephony.
why: Production-grade turn detection, interruptions and phone calls. It powers ChatGPT voice.

name: Pipecat
description: Open-source framework for voice and multimodal conversational agents.
why: Very flexible pipeline model with the widest range of STT, LLM and TTS integrations.

name: faster-whisper
description: Whisper speech recognition up to 4x faster with CTranslate2.
why: The practical way to run Whisper yourself: same accuracy, much faster and lighter.

name: ElevenLabs
description: Lifelike text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing and conversational voice agents.
why: The quality benchmark for synthetic voices.

name: Kokoro TTS
description: Small (82M) open-weight text-to-speech model with surprisingly high quality.
why: Near-commercial voice quality that runs on a CPU, for free.

name: ComfyUI
description: Node-based UI and backend for image and video diffusion models.
why: The power-user standard for local image and video generation workflows.

name: n8n
description: Workflow automation with 400+ integrations and native AI agent nodes; self-host or cloud.
why: Connects AI to all the apps you already use, with code when you need it. Self-hostable.
bestFor: connect ai to gmail slack sheets

name: Dify
description: Visual platform for building agentic workflows, RAG apps and chatbots.
why: The most complete visual LLM app platform: RAG, agents, monitoring and an API, self-hostable.

name: Langflow
description: Visual builder for agents and RAG flows; export as an API or MCP server.
why: Prototype visually, then ship the same flow as an API or MCP server.

name: Anthropic Skills
description: Anthropic's official skills: Word, PDF, PowerPoint and Excel files, frontend design, web-app testing, MCP builder, skill creator and more.
why: The reference examples of the format, and several are useful every day, like frontend-design and the document skills.
bestFor: create word excel powerpoint with ai
learn how to write a skill

learn.title: Anthropic: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills

name: skills (npx skills)
description: Vercel's open CLI for installing agent skills from any repo into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more.
why: One install command that works across agents; most skill repos document it as the default way to install.

name: Dembrandt Skills
description: 45 UX and design-system skills: WCAG 2.2, usability heuristics, type scales, button states, forms, information architecture and more.
why: Encodes senior UX judgment with cited standards, and agents load only the skill a prompt needs. Pairs with Dembrandt.

name: App Store Screenshots
description: Agent skill that scaffolds a Next.js editor for App Store and Google Play marketing screenshots, with device frames and exact-size export.
why: Turns raw simulator captures into store-ready screenshot sets in every required size, as a project you can edit and keep in git.

name: genjutsu
description: Creative-coding skills for motion, micro-interactions and design systems: web (GSAP, Three.js, CSS), SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.
why: Makes the agent propose an interaction plan you approve before it codes, and publishes full transcripts and costs of real runs.

name: Responsively App
description: Dev browser that shows your site on many device sizes side by side, with synced scrolling, clicks and typing.
why: AI generates UI fast; this is the fastest way to check it on every screen size at once.
bestFor: preview website on mobile and desktop
test ai generated ui on devices

name: Elicit
description: AI research assistant that finds academic papers, extracts data into tables and summarizes findings.
why: Built for literature reviews: it searches papers, not the open web, and extracts structured data you can check.

name: AlphaFold Server
description: Google DeepMind's free web service for AlphaFold 3: predicts structures of proteins and their complexes with DNA, RNA and ligands.
why: Nobel-recognized structure prediction in a browser, with no setup or GPU. Free for non-commercial research.

name: Boltz
description: Open-source biomolecular structure models; Boltz-2 adds binding-affinity prediction.
why: An MIT-licensed alternative to AlphaFold 3 that you can run yourself and use commercially.

name: Llama Guard
description: Meta's open safety classifiers for prompts and responses (Purple Llama).
why: A free, self-hostable moderation model that you can tune to your own policy.

name: NeMo Guardrails
description: NVIDIA toolkit for programmable rails on conversational systems.
why: Declarative rules for keeping a chatbot on topic and on policy.

name: garak
description: NVIDIA's LLM vulnerability scanner that probes for jailbreaks, prompt injection and data leaks.
why: Like nmap for LLMs: an automated security scan before launch.

name: uv
description: Extremely fast Python package and project manager in Rust.
why: Fixes Python environment pain. 10-100x faster than pip, and most AI repos now use it.

name: PyTorch
description: The dominant deep learning framework for research and production.
why: Almost every open model is built and released in PyTorch first.

name: Transformers
description: Hugging Face's library of pretrained models for text, vision and audio.
why: The universal model-definition library. If a model exists, it loads here.
bestFor: run hugging face model in python

name: Jupyter
description: Notebooks that keep code, data and results together; the default workspace for data science and research.
why: Where most data and ML work happens, and coding agents can read and edit notebooks too.
